Odisha At A Glance
01
Overview of Odisha
Raw, Real and Remarkable

Stretching along nearly 480 km of the Bay of Bengal, Odisha brings together sacred heritage and unspoiled natural beauty in a way few destinations can. From intricately carved stone temples and living cultural traditions to serene beaches, forested hills and thriving wildlife habitats the state offers an authentic travel experience shaped by centuries of history and enduring spirituality.

Across temple towns, craft villages, wetlands and coastal landscapes, Odisha unfolds as a destination where culture, nature and faith exist in seamless harmony inviting travellers to experience a way of life where tradition continues to shape the present.

WHAT MAKES ODISHA UNIQUE

Expansive eastern coastline with pristine and lesser explored beaches
Bhubaneswar the Temple City with hundreds of ancient shrines
Strong roots in an ancient maritime civilization
Globally admired temple architecture and stone craftsmanship
Ideal destination for slow, immersive and mindful travel
02
History & Civilization
A legacy shaped by time, faith and artistic excellence

With over two millennia of recorded history, Odisha stands among India’s most ancient cultural regions. The transformation of Emperor Ashoka after the historic Kalinga War marked a defining moment in world history spreading the philosophy of peace far beyond India.

Successive dynasties fostered a rich legacy of art, architecture, literature and religion many of which continue to thrive making Odisha a rare example of a civilization that is both historic and living.

HISTORICAL MILESTONES
Flourishing ancient maritime trade with Southeast Asia and beyond
The Kalinga War and its lasting global impact
Coexistence of Hindu, Buddhist and Jain traditions
Golden era of temple architecture (7th–13th century)
Continuity of age old customs and rituals
03
Geography, Climate & Ecology
From coastline to highlands a landscape of remarkable diversity

Odisha’s geography spans fertile river deltas, scenic coastlines, rolling plateaus and forested hills of the Eastern Ghats. Its rivers sustain agriculture and ecosystems while forests and wetlands support rich biodiversity.

Natural landmarks such as Chilika Lake, Similipal National Park and Bhitarkanika National Park highlight the state’s ecological significance making it a compelling destination for nature and wildlife enthusiasts.

GEOGRAPHY & LANDSCAPE AT A GLANCE
Nearly 574 km of coastline with beaches, estuaries and lagoons
Major river systems forming fertile plains and wetlands
Dense forests and biodiversity rich reserves
Tropical climate with summer, monsoon and winter seasons
Best time to visit: October to February
04
People, Languages & Living Traditions
A culture that is lived, celebrated and continuously evolving

The essence of Odisha lies in its people whose warmth reflects a deeply rooted cultural identity. The state is home to diverse indigenous communities each preserving unique languages, traditions and ways of life.

Here festivals, crafts, music and dance are not mere occasions they are integral to daily life making Odisha’s culture dynamic, inclusive and deeply experiential.

CULTURAL INSIGHTS & HERITAGE
Odia - One of India’s classical languages
A rich diversity of indigenous and tribal communities
Strong deep-rooted traditions of classical and folk arts
A vibrant calendar of festivals aligned with seasons, agriculture and temple rituals
Renowned traditional crafts including handloom textiles, Pattachitra and silver filigree

Iconic Odisha
TIMELESS TEMPLES, EPIC LANDSCAPES AND LIVING TRADITIONS — DISCOVER THE ICONS OF ODISHA.
/
Discover
/
Iconic Odisha
01
Shree Jagannath Temple, Puri
The spiritual heartbeat of Odisha.

One of India’s most revered pilgrimage sites Shree Mandir better known as the Jagannath Temple to the outside world in Puri is the epicentre of Odisha’s spiritual and cultural life. Built in the 12th century by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deba the temple is dedicated to Lord Jagannath, worshipped alongside his siblings Lord Balabhadra and Debi Subhadra.

Its towering temple dominates the sacred skyline of Puri and has drawn devotees from across the world for centuries. The temple is especially famous for the grand Ratha Jatra or Chariot Festival as it is known worldwide. Massive wooden chariots carry the deities through the streets in a spectacle witnessed by millions.

The temple kitchen considered among the largest in the world prepares Mahaprasad using traditional cooking methods passed down through generations.

WHY IS IT ICONIC
One of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites in India
World famous Ratha Jatra festival
Unique Jagannath culture and rituals
Home to the largest temple kitchen serving Mahaprasad
02
Sun Temple, Konark
Where Time Rides on the Chariot of the Sun God.

The Sun Temple at Konark is one of India’s most extraordinary architectural masterpieces. Built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty the temple was designed as a colossal chariot dedicated to Surya, the Sun God.

The monument features intricately carved stone wheels, pillars and sculptures that showcase the brilliance of medieval craftsmanship. Each wheel of the chariot represents the passage of time and functions as a sundial.

Recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the temple remains a powerful symbol of Odisha’s artistic and architectural excellence.

WHY IS IT ICONIC
UNESCO World Heritage Site
Temple shaped like the Sun God’s celestial chariot
The famous stone wheels that function as sundials
It represents the pinnacle of Kalingan temple architecture
The temple is a masterpiece of artistic and scientific confluence
03
Ekamra Kshetra, Bhubaneswar
Where A Thousand Temples Tell A Timeless Story

In the heart of Bhubaneswar lies Ekamra Kshetra or Old Town as it is commonly called a timeless sacred landscape where the rhythm of life feels strikingly different from the city’s fast paced modern avenues.

Around the serene waters of Bindu Sagar Lake priests chant morning prayers families quietly perform rituals for their ancestors and residents go about their daily chores amid centuries old temples that shape the skyline.

At the centre rises the towering Lingaraj Temple watching over a neighbourhood where time seems to slow down. While the rest of Bhubaneswar moves with the energy of a growing modern city, Old Town continues at its own gentle pace here heritage is not preserved behind walls but lived every single day.

WHY IS IT ICONIC
Living Temple City: Unlike archaeological ruins Ekamra Kshetra is a living functional heritage site where centuries old traditions continue alongside modern life.
Epicentre of Kalinga Architecture: It showcases the complete evolution of the Kalinga style with the 11th century, 128-foot high Lingaraj Temple being the most prominent alongside Mukteswar, Rajarani and Ananta Basudeb temples.
Historical & Spiritual Continuity: It spans over 2,000 years of history (3rd Century BC to 15th Century AD), including sites related to Buddhism (Ashokan Rock Edicts at Dhauli), Jainism (Udaygiri-Khandagiri) and Hinduism.
04
Chilika Lake
Where Rivers Meet the Sea and Wings Fill the Sky

Chilika is more than a lake it is a living landscape where river meets sea and freshwater blends with saltwater. Spread across the districts of Puri, Khordha and Ganjam it is Asia’s largest brackish water lagoon.

Fed by dozens of rivers and linked to the Bay of Bengal, Chilika constantly shifts with the seasons, shaping islands, wetlands and rich biodiversity.

Recognised as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance it is one of Odisha’s greatest natural wonders.

WHY CHILIKA IS ICONIC
Asia’s Largest Brackish Water Lagoon - Where freshwater rivers merge with the tidal waters of the Bay of Bengal creating a unique and highly productive ecosystem.
A Global Birding Destination - Every winter more than a million migratory birds arrive from regions as distant as Siberia, Central Asia and the Himalayas.
Home of the Irrawaddy Dolphin - Chilika supports one of the largest lagoon populations of the endangered Irrawaddy dolphin in the world.
A Living Cultural Landscape - Sacred temples, fishing traditions and festivals are deeply intertwined with the rhythm of the lagoon.
A Conservation Success Story – Community led restoration efforts helped revive the lake’s ecology making Chilika an internationally recognised example of wetland conservation.
05
Similipal National Park
Where deep forests, roaring waterfalls and rare black tigers thrive

Located in Mayurbhanj district, Similipal is one of India’s most remarkable forest landscapes and a cornerstone of Odisha’s wilderness. It was among the first nine reserves brought under Project Tiger in 1973 and today forms part of the Similipal Tiger Reserve and Biosphere Reserve protecting rich biodiversity within the Eastern Ghats. Dense sal forests, rolling hills and wild orchids the red simul cotton trees after which it gets its name and winding rivers define this vast wilderness. Similipal is also the only place in the world where the rare Melanistic (black) Tiger has been recorded in the wild. Alongside Royal Bengal tigers, the forests support elephants, gaurs, leopards, mugger crocodiles and a remarkable variety of birds and reptiles. The reserve is equally famous for its dramatic waterfalls Barehipani, India’s second highest waterfall and the majestic Joranda Falls cascading through deep forested valleys. For travellers seeking raw nature and wildlife, Similipal reveals Odisha at its wildest.

WHY IS IT ICONIC
Among the first nine Tiger Reserves under Project Tiger (1973)
Only known habitat of the rare Melanistic (black) Tiger
Home to spectacular waterfalls like Barehipani and Joranda
One of India’s richest biodiversity landscapes in the Eastern Ghats
Home to numerous indigenous communities, such as the Mankidia and Santals, who live in harmony with nature an

Heritage & Architecture
ETERNAL KALINGA – STORIES CARVED IN EVERY DETAIL

Heritage & Architecture
01
Kalinga Temple Architecture
A timeless design language shaped by devotion, precision and artistry

Kalinga temple architecture which flourished between the 7th and 13th centuries represents one of India’s most refined sacred design traditions. Defined by soaring curvilinear towers, intricate carvings and harmonious proportions, these temples transform stone into a powerful expression of faith.

Iconic structures such as the Sun Temple at Konark, the Jagannath Temple in Puri and the Lingaraj Temple exemplify this architectural brilliance where every detail from sculpted walls to spatial planning reflects both artistic mastery and spiritual intent.

ARCHITECTURAL FEATURES
Distinct temple style unique to Odisha
Towering spires (Deul) and intricately carved façades
Classical four-part structural composition
Sculptural storytelling inspired by mythology and daily life
Use of sacred geometry and precise alignment
02
Sacred & Monastic Architecture
Spaces of faith, learning and spiritual evolution

Odisha’s architectural legacy reflects a rare confluence of spiritual traditions. From grand temples to rock-cut caves and monastic universities these spaces served not only as centres of worship but also as hubs of learning and philosophical exchange.

The Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves reveal early Jain ascetic traditions through their rock-cut forms, while the Buddhist sites of Ratnagiri, Lalitgiri and Udayagiri  collectively known as the Diamond Triangle once thrived as major centres of Mahayana and Vajrayana learning, attracting scholars from across Asia.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS
Coexistence of Hindu, Buddhist and Jain architectural traditions
Rock-cut caves, monasteries, stupas and meditation spaces
Centres of ancient learning and spiritual discourse
Archaeological remains of global significance
Where the sacred spaces where deeply integrated with the landscape and not imposed on it.
03
Ancient & Medieval Monuments
Enduring landmarks of power, vision and engineering brilliance

Across Odisha, monuments stand as enduring records of dynasties, innovation and cultural evolution. The Sun Temple at Konark, often called the Black Pagoda, is a masterpiece of 13th-century engineering and cosmic symbolism. Similarly, Dhauli marks a historic turning point that reshaped the course of Indian and world history.

The Hathigumpha Inscription at the Udaygiri Caves is one of the most vital primary sources for ancient Indian history, providing a rare year-by-year account of a ruler’s achievements during the 1st or 2nd century BCE.

The image used is of the Hathigumpha, Udaygiri Caves and the information displayed should reflect the above historical context in the text portion.

MONUMENT HIGHLIGHTS
Globally recognised heritage landmarks
Early inscriptions of political and spiritual significance
Remnants of ancient forts and urban centres
Advanced engineering and astronomical alignment
Architectural expressions of power and devotion
04
Museums & Interpretation Centres
Preserving the past, enriching the present

Odisha’s museums and interpretation centres offer deeper insight into its layered heritage. Housing rare manuscripts, sculptures, textiles and tribal artefacts they connect visitors with the stories behind the monuments.

Spaces such as the Odisha State Museum, Tribal Museum, Kala Bhoomi, ASI Museum at Konark and the Netaji Birthplace Museum, Kataka transform history into an engaging and accessible experience.

WHAT YOU’LL DISCOVER
Rare artefacts and palm-leaf manuscripts
Tribal art, textiles and craft traditions
Sculptures preserved from heritage sites
Curated galleries and interpretive displays
Insights into maritime and cultural history

state.content:

Spiritual & Sacred Odisha
DIVINE ODISHA — WHERE FAITH LIVES IN EVERY MOMENT
/
Discover
/
Spiritual & Sacred Odisha
01
Jagannath Culture and Traditions
A living philosophy of inclusivity, devotion and shared faith

At the heart of Odisha’s spiritual identity lies the Holy Trinity of Puri - Lord Jagannath, Lord Balabhadra and Devi Subhadra. Beyond being worshipped as deities, they represent universal acceptance that transcends social and cultural boundaries. 

Figures like Salabega, the Muslim poet-saint and saints such as Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Guru Nanak and Kabir have all found deep resonance here. Worship combines rituals, sacred food offerings, music, festivals and community participation. The Ratha Jatra where the deities step out among devotees stands as a powerful symbol of equality.

CULTURAL ESSENCE
Ancient rituals preserved through generations
World-famous Ratha Jatra celebrating inclusivity
Mahaprasad as a shared community offering
Temple arts, music and devotional traditions
A living, accessible spiritual heritage
02
Major Temples & Sacred Centres
Sacred geographies shaped by devotion and continuity

Odisha’s spiritual landscape includes ancient temple towns, Shakti Peethas and sacred hills that continue to draw pilgrims. Bhubaneswar’s Ekamra Kshetra, with hundreds of shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva, is one of India’s oldest living temple traditions.

Key sacred sites include Maa Samaleswari in Sambalpur the stunning black chlorite temple of Maa Kichakeswari in Khiching the hilltop shrine of Tara Tarini and the mythologically rich scenic mountain of Mahendragiri.

PILGRIMAGE POWER CENTRES
Renowned temples and Shakti Peethas across regions
Ekamra Kshetra as a living temple heritage zone
Strong continuity of rituals and daily worship practices
Deep mythological, historical and regional significance
Sacred landscapes blending nature and spirituality
03
Buddhist Sites
Landscapes of transformation, learning and peace

Odisha played a key role in Buddhist history following Emperor Ashoka’s transformation after the Kalinga War. Dhauli, with its peace pagoda and rock-cut inscriptions, stands as a powerful symbol of peace and spiritual awakening.

Along with the monastic complexes of Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri, these sites form a historic circuit of learning and meditation that once attracted scholars from across Asia.

BUDDHIST CIRCUIT
Ancient monastic universities and learning centres
Archaeological remains of Buddhist heritage
Peace monuments and historic inscriptions
Important pilgrimage and meditation sites
Serene environment for spiritual reflection
04
Sacred Water Bodies and Ritual Spaces
Where water becomes a medium of faith and purification

Sacred ponds and ghats, such as Bindu Sagar in Bhubaneswar and Narendra Tank in Puri are integral to temple rituals and festivals. They symbolise purification, devotion and the deep connection between water and divinity.

SACRED WATER HERITAGE
Ritual cleansing as part of worship traditions
Integral to temple festivals and processions
Symbolic connection between water and spirituality
Historic temple-tank architectural systems
Spaces for quiet reflection and community rituals
05
Festivals and Living Traditions
When devotion transforms into collective celebration

Spirituality in Odisha comes alive through festivals rooted in devotion, seasonal cycles and community participation. Ratha Jatra in Puri is a global symbol of faith, while Boita Bandana and Bali Jatra honour maritime traditions. Nuakhai celebrates the harvest, Raja Parba marks womanhood and Danda Nata reflects penance and devotion.

LIVING TRADITIONS
Ratha Jatra as a global symbol of devotion and equality
Festivals linked to agriculture, seasons and heritage
Ritual performances expressing penance and faith
Strong community participation across regions
Continuity of traditions in everyday life

Wildlife Sanctuaries of Odisha
PROTECTED HABITATS PRESERVING ODISHA’S WILD HERITAGE
/
Discover
/
Wildlife Sanctuaries of Odisha
01
NATIONAL PARKS & SANCTUARIES
Where Every Forest Tells a Story

Odisha’s network of national parks and wildlife sanctuaries safeguards diverse ecosystems, ranging from dense sal forests to river valleys and grasslands. These protected areas support thriving populations of elephants, deer, reptiles and numerous bird species, while promoting responsible eco-tourism through guided trails and conservation awareness experiences.

HIGHLIGHTS
Major protected forest ecosystems
Elephant migration corridors
Reptile and bird habitats
Guided safaris & interpretation trails
Community-based conservation initiatives
02
TIGER RESERVES & BIOSPHERE ZONES
Into the Core Wilderness of India’s Iconic Predators.

Odisha hosts important tiger reserves and biosphere zones where entire ecological systems remain preserved in natural balance. These landscapes protect apex predators and their habitats while allowing carefully regulated wildlife tourism and research activities.

HIGHLIGHTS
Tiger conservation habitats
Pristine forest biodiversity zones
Regulated wildlife safaris
Research and conservation programs
High ecological diversity regions
03
WATERFALLS, HILLS & FORESTS
Scenic Highlands Shaped by Nature and Seasons.

The Eastern Ghats form Odisha’s dramatic landscape of forested hills, valleys and seasonal waterfalls. These landscapes offer trekking routes, panoramic viewpoints and immersive slow-travel experiences across changing seasonal colours. 

HIGHLIGHTS
Mountain and plateau landscapes
Seasonal waterfalls and streams
Sunrise & sunset viewpoints
Trekking and nature trails
Landscape photography locations
04
WETLANDS & MANGROVES
Coastal Ecosystems alive with Water and Migration.

Odisha’s wetlands, lagoons and mangrove forests are among South Asia’s significant coastal biodiversity habitats. They support rich marine life, migratory birds while protecting the coastline and traditional fishing communities.

HIGHLIGHTS
Lagoons and estuarine ecosystems
Mangrove and tidal forests
Marine biodiversity habitats
Bird nesting grounds
Sustainable coastal livelihoods
05
BIRDING IN ODISHA
Every Season, A New Discovery

Odisha's wetlands situated on the Central Asian Flyway welcome millions of migratory birds as a winter refuge. Every Season, A New Discovery. Located along the Central Asian Flyway, Odisha transforms into a vital winter refuge for over a million migratory birds. Between October and March, wetlands such as Chilika Lagoon and Hirakud Reservoir attract birdwatchers, photographers and researchers to witness this vibrant natural spectacle throughout the year. 

HIGHLIGHTS
Migratory and resident bird hotspots across wetlands and coastal areas
Rare and endangered species sightings throughout the year
Wetland and lagoon bird habitats for immersive observation
Guided birdwatching and photography experiences
Seasonal diversity ensuring new discoveries in every visit
06
LAKE TRAILS
Water Landscapes Shaped by Migration, Community and Calm.

Odisha’s lakes range from the vast brackish Chilika lagoon to quiet inland freshwater reservoirs. These wetlands support migratory birds, aquatic life and traditional fishing communities offering peaceful journeys where nature and local culture exist together in harmony.

HIGHLIGHTS
Lagoon, wetland and freshwater ecosystems
Migratory bird observation zones
Boating and shoreline walks
Fishing communities and cultural landscapes
Sunrise, sunset and photography viewpoints
07
NATURE TRAILS
Walk Through Landscapes Where Biodiversity Still Leads the Way.

Nature trails across Odisha pass through dense sal forests, mangrove swamps, scenic river valleys and the Eastern Ghats hills. Guided paths allow visitors to observe wildlife, seasonal vegetation and natural ecosystems through responsible eco-travel experiences. 

HIGHLIGHTS
Forest trekking and eco-walking paths
Wildlife observation areas
River, mangrove and hill ecosystems
Nature camps and guided trails (Similipal, Debrigarh)
Responsible eco-tourism experiences
08
CONSERVATION & SUCCESS STORIES
Odisha Leads the Way in Nature Conservation

The state’s forests, wetlands and coastal ecosystems are not just habitats they are living laboratories of conservation. Through innovative community initiatives, strict protection policies and long-term ecological planning, Odisha has achieved remarkable success in preserving biodiversity while enabling sustainable tourism.

HIGHLIGHTS
Forest Cover - Nearly one-third of Odisha is forested, supporting exceptional biodiversity
Saltwater Crocodiles - Bhitarkanika hosts one of India’s largest populations due to long-term conservation.
Mangalajodi - Transformed from a poaching hotspot into a globally recognised community-led bird sanctuary.
Chilika Lake - Restoration efforts have revived migratory bird populations and rare Irrawaddy dolphins.
Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary - Offers unique safaris along the Hirakud reservoir with sightings of Indian bison, deer and rich birdlife.

UNTOUCHED SHORES — BEYOND THE USUAL COASTLINES
/

Coastal Getaway
01
COASTAL HIGHLIGHTS
Natural beauty, culture and tranquillity along Odisha’s shores

Stretching along the Bay of Bengal, Odisha’s coastline offers a refreshing escape from crowded beach destinations. Here golden sands meet open skies, fishing villages coexist with serene shores and every sunrise feels personal. From lively coastal hubs to quiet, unexplored stretches, Odisha provides beach experiences that are both vibrant and peaceful perfect for travellers seeking space, simplicity and authenticity.

HIGHLIGHTS
Sunrise Coastline - Among India’s best places to witness breathtaking sunrises
Uncrowded Beaches - Miles of clean, less-commercialised shores for solitude and relaxation
Coastal Culture - Fishing villages, local cuisine, and temple traditions shape daily life
Unique Ecosystems - Olive Ridley turtle nesting sites and coastal biodiversity
02
SIGNATURE BEACH EXPERIENCES
Vibrant, serene and authentic seaside escapes

Odisha’s beaches offer diverse experiences, from spiritual hubs to quiet retreats. The beaches are defined by its scenic landscapes, local communities and unique ecosystems.

HIGHLIGHTS
Puri Beach - Blends spirituality, local life and ocean views in a lively seaside setting
Gopalpur Beach - Quiet coastal town with old-world charm and relaxed vibes
Astaranga Beach - Known for colourful sunsets and bustling fishing harbour
03
COASTAL NATURE & CONSERVATION
Preserving ecosystems while embracing the sea

Odisha’s coastline is not only scenic but ecologically significant.

HIGHLIGHTS
Olive Ridley Turtles - Witness one of the world’s largest mass nesting events along Rushikulya and Gahirmatha
Chilika Lagoon (Satapada) - Where the sea meets the lagoon home to the rare Irrawaddy dolphin
Sustainable Coastal Life - Local communities actively protect marine ecosystems and biodiversity
Eco-Tourism Practices - Responsible travel initiatives ensuring minimal impact on beaches and marine life

Tribes of Odisha
ROOTED IN NATURE — LIVING TRADITIONS, TIMELESS WISDOM

Tribal Odisha
01
TRIBAL COMMUNITIES OF ODISHA
Diverse cultures thriving in harmony with nature

In Odisha tribal life is not just a cultural identity it is a way of living in harmony with nature. Home to over 60 tribal communities, each with its own identity, rituals and traditions, it is one of India’s largest and most diverse tribal populations. The state offers a rare window into communities that have preserved their traditions, knowledge systems and ways of life over centuries. From forested highlands to remote valleys, these communities celebrate life through rituals, music, markets and an intrinsic connection with the land. Some of the distinctive tribes are mentioned below.

HIGHLIGHTS
Bonda - Distinctive attire and strong cultural identity
Dongria Kondh - Deeply connected to the sacred Niyamgiri Hills
Santhal - Celebrated for vibrant music, dance and community life
Saura - Known for ritual art and spiritual traditions
Gadaba & Paraja - Rooted in agriculture and age-old cultural practices
02
WAY OF LIFE
Simplicity, sustainability and community at the heart

Life in tribal Odisha revolves around respect for nature, shared responsibility and ancient knowledge systems.

HIGHLIGHTS
Deep respect for forests, hills and natural cycles
Homes built using locally sourced sustainable materials
Food habits based on seasonal and forest produce
Oral traditions for passing knowledge and culture
Balanced living that remains relevant today
03
MARKETS & CULTURAL EXCHANGE (HAATS)
Living culture through trade and interaction

Weekly tribal markets, or haats, especially in Koraput and Malkangiri, offer visitors a glimpse into authentic tribal life.

HIGHLIGHTS
Vibrant spaces for local produce, forest goods, and essentials
Interaction and cultural exchange with communities
Insight into traditional economic and social systems
A raw, real, and immersive visitor experience
04
TRIBAL ART & EXPRESSION
Creative traditions rooted in belief, nature, and daily life

Art, craft, music and dance in Odisha’s tribal communities are living, evolving traditions rather than museum exhibits.

HIGHLIGHTS
Saura Paintings - Ritualistic wall art depicting deities, ancestors and daily life
Dokra Metal Craft - Ancient lost-wax casting from Mayurbhanj, Dhenkanal and Sundaragada, producing figurines, jewellery and decor with raw, intricate detailing
Kotpad Weave - Handloom textiles from southern Odisha, dyed with natural roots, earthy tones and distinct cultural significance
Music & Dance - Integral to festivals, rituals and communal celebrations, reflecting joy, devotion and identity
05
WHERE TO EXPERIENCE
Heartlands of tribal culture and landscapes

The highlands of Koraput, Malkangiri, Rayagada, Mayurbhanj and Phulbani are the cultural heartlands of Odisha, where tribal traditions, landscapes and weekly haats create authentic experiences for visitors.

HIGHLIGHTS
Deeply rooted tribal belts with rich culture and natural beauty
Opportunities to witness daily life, crafts and rituals
Immersive eco-cultural experiences guided by local communities
Landscapes ranging from forested hills to river valleys

/

Arts, Crafts & Handloom
01
CRAFT TRADITIONS OF ODISHA
Where Art thrives in Workshops, Homes and Artisan Villages

Passed down through generations, the state’s rich legacy of handicrafts and textiles reflects a deep connection between culture, creativity and skilled craftsmanship.

HIGHLIGHTS
Pattachitra Painting - Intricate, mythological narratives in natural colours, practised in heritage villages like Raghurajpur
Silver Filigree (Tarakasi) - Delicate jewellery and ornamental pieces crafted from fine silver wires centred in Kataka
Stone & Wood Carving - Detailed sculptures inspired by temple architecture and traditional motifs
Applique Work (Pipili) - Vibrant textiles with bold patterns, used in temple canopies, umbrellas and festive décor
Sabai Grass Craft - Eco-friendly weaving from Mayurbhanj producing baskets, mats and lifestyle products
Dokra Metal Craft - Tribal-inspired lost-wax metal casting with rustic finishes, practiced in Dhenkanal, Mayurbhanj and Sundaragada
02
TEXTILES & HANDLOOMS
Fabric traditions reflecting Odisha’s culture and identity

Heritage preserved through skill, colour and creativity-Odisha’s textile heritage is renowned for its craftsmanship, natural dyes and distinctive motifs.

HIGHLIGHTS
Sambalpuri Ikat - Globally admired for intricate tie-dye technique and geometric precision
Bomkai Sarees - Unique blend of traditional motifs and contemporary design
Kotpad Textiles - Naturally dyed fabrics with earthy tones from the highlands of southern Odisha
Brahmapuri Patta Sarees - Elegant silk sarees with fine texture, temple-inspired borders and distinct Odia identity
03
CRAFT HUBS & ARTISAN VILLAGES
Communities where traditions thrive

Odisha’s artisans continue to practice centuries-old crafts that showcase precision, storytelling and cultural identity. The crafts flourish in dedicated clusters, where visitors can witness the making process and interact with artisans.

HIGHLIGHTS
Raghurajpur - Heritage crafts village renowned for Pattachitra, Palm leaf, engravings and traditional art forms
Kataka - Centre of silver filigree (Tarakasi) craftsmanship
Pipili - Famous for vibrant applique work and craft markets
Sambalpur & Baragada - Renowned for traditional Sambalpuri handloom weaving traditions
Brahmapur - Brahmapuri Patta silk sarees and weaving heritage
Mayurbhanj - Sabai grass craft, Dokra metalwork and tribal art forms

state.content:

Festivals & Celebrations
WHERE CULTURE COMES ALIVE IN COMMUNITY
/
Experience
/
Festival & Celebrations
STEP INTO A CALENDAR OF CELEBRATIONS SHAPED BY RITUAL, TRADITION AND THE SPIRIT OF TOGETHERNESS
Celebrating Life
Celebrate timeless traditions through festivals that unite communities, where culture, rituals and joyous moments come alive for every traveller.
SPIRITUAL FESTIVAL | PURI
Ratha Jatra

Experience or Witness one of the world’s largest religious gatherings as massive chariots roll through the streets, drawing millions into a shared moment of devotion and energy. 

CULTURAL & HISTORIC FESTIVAL | KATAKA
Boita Bandana & Bali Jatra

Celebrate Odisha’s maritime legacy through riverbank rituals and one of the region’s largest fairs, which comes alive with crafts, cultural performances and local cuisine.

CULTURAL FESTIVAL | KONARK
Konark Festival

Held at the iconic Sun Temple of Konark, the Konark Dance Festival showcases Indian classical dance and music with renowned artists performing Odissi and other forms under the open sky, blending heritage, art and architecture.

RELIGIOUS & CULTURAL FESTIVAL | STATEWIDE
Durga Puja (Dussehra)

Odisha’s Durga Puja is known for its artistic grandeur and community spirit. From silver-adorned pandals in Kataka to powerful Shakti worship in Puri and across western Odisha, the festival reflects devotion expressed through craftsmanship and celebration. 

FOLK THEATRE FESTIVAL | BARAGADA
Dhanu Jatra

Every year, Baragada turns into the mythological kingdom of Mathura for Dhanu Jatra. From the grand Kansa Durbar (the Court of King Kansa) to the streets across the town, scenes from Krishna Leela are performed live, with artists and locals bringing the story to life. This remarkable celebration is recognised as one of the world's largest open-air theatre festivals.

Regional & Seasonal Festivals- Beyond the Big Celebrations

Away from iconic events, Odisha’s cultural richness comes alive in regional and seasonal traditions:

Cultural Festival | Western Odisha
Nuakhai - A major harvest festival celebrating new rice, family bonding and community solidarity in Western Odisha
Seasonal Festival | Coastal Odisha
Raja Parba - A three-day festival celebrating womanhood and the onset of monsoon, featuring swings, traditional food and leisure.
Cultural Festival | Southern Odisha
Budhi Thakurani Jatra - A vibrant biennial festival in Ganjam marking the ceremonial visit of the goddess to her maternal home, featuring masked dances, street processions and night-long performances.
Folk Dance Festival | Mayurbhanj
The Chhau Festival celebrates Odisha’s masked dance tradition, blending martial movements, mythology, and tribal folk heritage.

state.content:

EN

Cuisine & Culinary Trails
EXPERIENCE ODISHA THROUGH ITS FLAVOURS.
/
Experience
/
Cuisine & Culinary Trails
SAVOUR A RICH TAPESTRY OF FLAVOURS ROOTED IN RITUAL, LANDSCAPE AND CENTURIES-OLD CULINARY WISDOM
Cuisine and Culinary Trails

Food in Odisha is more than just a meal it’s a reflection of tradition, community and daily life. From temple kitchens and coastal homes to bustling city streets, every dish tells a story rooted in simplicity, seasonality and deep cultural connections. 

Whether you’re sharing a traditional meal, tasting fresh seafood by the coast or exploring local street food, Odisha offers a culinary journey that is both authentic and diverse

Temple Food Experience

One of the most unique culinary experiences in Odisha is the Mahaprasad of Puri. The abhada (Prasad) at Ananta Basudeb Temple in Ekamra Kshetra, Bhubaneswar, is something to savour too.

Cooked in traditional earthen pots over firewood.
Prepared in one of the world’s largest temple kitchens.
Shared by thousands in a spirit of equality and community.
It is not just food it is a deeply spiritual and cultural experience.
Coastal & Seafood Trails

With a long coastline and access to the brackish waters of Chilika Lake, Odisha offers fresh and flavourful seafood. 

Prawns, crabs, and fish prepared with local spices.
Beachside dining in places like Puri, Chilika, Baleshwar and Gopalpur.
A perfect blend of simplicity and bold coastal flavours.
Rural & Traditional Cuisine

At the heart of Odia cuisine lies its connection to the land. Meals are seasonal, balanced, and designed around local ingredients.

Pakhala - A cooling, fermented rice dish perfect for warm climates.
Dalma - A wholesome mix of lentils and vegetables.
Parched Rice and Puffed Rice-based dishes - Simple, nutritious and deeply rooted in tradition. Mayurbhanj is famous for its Mudhi (Puffed Rice) Mansa (Mutton).
Pitha - Traditional Odia delicacies made from rice flour with a variety of fillings, ranging from sweet coconut and jaggery to spiced lentils. Savoured across festivals and daily life, they are a symbol of Odisha’s culinary heritage and seasonal celebrations.
Bamboo & Patra Poda Delicacies - Rooted in traditional methods, Bamboo Mutton, Chicken and Mushrooms are slow-cooked in bamboo over fire, while Patra Poda dishes are marinated, wrapped in leaves and roasted. The result is a smoky, aromatic flavour that reflects Odisha’s tribal culinary heritage and close connection with nature.
Street Food & City Bites

Cities like Bhubaneswar, Kataka and Brahmapur offer a vibrant street food culture.

Dahi Bara Aloo Dum - A local favourite with a distinctive flavour profile, originally from Kataka and now widely popular across Odisha.
A variety of rolls, chaats and quick bites influenced by regional tastes.
Bustling food streets that come alive in the evenings.
Sweet Trail

No culinary journey in Odisha is complete without its iconic sweets.

Chhena Poda - originally from Nayagada, this slow-baked dessert with a rich caramelised flavour is hugely popular.
Rasagola - Known as Kheera Mohan inside the Shree Mandir premises this Soft, syrupy sweet is very popular and deeply associated with Odisha’s heritage.
Khaja - A crispy, layered sweet traditionally associated with temple offerings. 
Chenna Jhili - Cottage Cheese Jalebi unique to Nimapada, a quaint town enroute Sun Temple at Konark, this sweet captures your palette like no other.
Sarsatia - A traditional sweet, unique to Sambalpur, made by weaving a flour paste into hot sugar syrup. Light, simple and not overly sweet it offers a unique texture and flavour.

Eco Tourism
SLOW DOWN. STAY CLOSE TO NATURE.
/
Experience
/
Ecotourism
SUSTAINABLE JOURNEYS
Experience Real Odisha

Odisha offers eco-tourism experiences that bring you closer to nature without disturbing its balance. From forest camps and riverside retreats to wetlands and coastal ecosystems, these journeys are designed to be immersive yet responsible.

Guided by conservation and supported by local communities, Odisha offers journeys that are slower, deeper and more meaningful. Rooted in nature, culture and community these experiences take you into forest landscapes, tribal villages and rural settings where life unfolds at its own rhythm. 

This is where travel becomes personal, grounded in simplicity, sustainability and genuine human connections.

COMFORT IN THE HEART OF NATURE
Eco Retreat Odisha (Seasonal- Dec to Feb)
Stays that immerse guests in nature, beaches, riversides, forests and hills
Comfortable accommodations designed with sustainability in mind
Curated experiences local cuisine, cultural evenings and traditions
Guided outdoor activities connecting guests to the landscape and wildlife
Community led initiatives ensuring authentic responsible tourism
STAY CLOSE TO WILDLIFE & WILDERNESS
Eco Tour Nature Camps
Odisha’s eco-tourism initiatives offer immersive stays in some of its most pristine natural landscapes.
Nature camps are set amidst forests, wetlands and wildlife habitats
Managed and operated by local communities creating sustainable livelihoods
Designed to offer authentic wilderness experiences with minimal environmental impact
From waking up to birdsong to experiencing life close to the wild, these stays are both refreshing and responsible.
EMPOWERING LOCAL ROOTS
Community Led Experiences
Eco Retreats (luxury glamping) and Eco Tour Nature Camps set across forests, rivers, wetlands and coastlines.
Operated with strong involvement of local communities creating sustainable livelihoods.
Guided experiences led by trained local experts with deep knowledge of the landscape.
Comfortable stays designed with eco-sensitive practices and minimal environmental impact.
Curated activities including nature trails, birdwatching, wildlife exploration and cultural interactions. 
TRAVEL WITH A PURPOSE
Responsible Travel
Sustainability is at the heart of these experiences.
Many eco destinations follow strict no plastic policies in places like Debrigarh, plastic is completely banned
Local communities continue to live with minimal reliance on plastic
Visitors are encouraged to reduce waste, respect nature and travel responsibly
Your choices help preserve these fragile ecosystems and support local livelihoods.
Respect local customs and engage with artisans supporting the preservation of traditional arts and crafts

Tribal, Village and Rural Life
EXPERIENCE ODISHA THROUGH ITS ROOTS
/
Experience
/
Tribal, Village & Rural Life
AUTHENTIC CONNECTIONS
Deepen Your Journey

Escape fast-paced itineraries for a slower, deeper and more meaningful journey through Odisha. Across tribal heartlands, rural landscapes and village settings life unfolds at its own rhythm deeply rooted in tradition, nature and everyday simplicity. 

This is where travel becomes more personal, shaped by authentic connections and a deeper sense of place. Experience the warm hospitality of local communities and immerse yourself in the timeless beauty of Odisha's rural soul.

CULTURAL HEARTLANDS
Tribal & Rural Experiences
The tribal belts of Mayurbhanj, Phulbani and Koraput offer some of the most authentic cultural experiences in Odisha.
Villages that reflect a deep connection with land, forests and tradition
Everyday life shaped by community, agriculture and nature
A chance to observe and understand living cultural practices
Villages like Bobeijoda, recognised as one of the cleanest in India, highlight the values of sustainability and mindful living. 
Shop authentic crafts and handlooms at government-run outlets like Utkalika and Boyanika.
LIVING TRADITIONS
Heritage Craft Villages
Villages like Raghurajpur and Pipili preserve centuries old craft traditions.
Home to master artisans practicing Pattachitra, applique and other traditional arts.
Every home double as a workshop keeping heritage alive through generations.
Visitors can witness live craft-making and interact directly with artisans.
A unique blend of culture, creativity and everyday village life.
Support local artisans by shopping at government run Utkalika and Boyanika outlets.
ROOTED IN NATURE
Village Life
Life revolves around agriculture, weaving and seasonal cycles where paddy fields and rivers shape the daily rhythm. 
Odisha, especially Western Odisha, is the heartland of Handloom specifically Sambalpuri textiles.
Generations of weavers continue age-old techniques with precision and pride.
A simple, grounded lifestyle deeply connected to land, craft and community.
Experience the stillness and beauty of rural landscapes that invite you to reconnect.
MINDFUL JOURNEYS
The Essence of Slow Travel
Travel here is not about ticking destinations it’s about experiencing moments.
Spending time in nature rather than rushing through it.
Engaging with local communities and their way of life.
Discovering the beauty of simplicity and stillness.
Odisha’s rural landscapes invite you to pause, observe and reconnect.
